items.value: soybean crush (ZS vs ZM and ZL): intraday cointegration at 1-minute sampling in the day session
items.window: calendar 2015, 243 trading days, CME LOB data
items.detail: Type: economic spread. Zhou, Bagnarosa, Gohin, Pennings, Debie (2023) J. Commodity Markets 30, 100314 (peer-reviewed; open-access copy). Day session (08:30-13:20 CT, 'session 2'), 1-minute data, missing-data filtered: cointegrated on 180 of 243 days (Table 2), 229 days at 2-minute sampling (NCCC-134 2022 version); Johansen without filtering only 64-70 days. Overnight 'session 1' (19:00-07:45 CT): 52 days (NCCC version Table 7). Speed of reversion related to volume and liquidity; stronger cointegration on USDA days. Horizon: minute-level, within-day. No half-life or trading test reported. In sample.
items.quote: A high level of cointegration is indeed observed during session 2 trading hours, which fades away during session 1. Another interesting result is the stronger intraday cointegration observed on average on USDA announcement days, although the number of observations available is limited.

source.field: text lines 744-747; Table 2 'Missing data filtered cointegration test ... ZS open interest rollover 180 11 3'

items.value: soybean crush: overnight session cointegration on 52 days vs 180 in the day session (1-minute, 2015)

items.quote: cointegration is mainly playing during session 2 (market official trading hours) of a trading day and significantly less so during session 1 (electronic trading hours). items.detail: Onur and Reiffen (CFTC working paper, Jan 2018) 'The Effect of Settlement Rules on the Incentive to Bang the Close'. Horizon: settlement minute to next-day open (overnight/daily, not intraday 5-min+). Before 2012-06-25 the settlement period was 13:14-13:15 CT (floor only). Evidence of a settlement-window effect that weakened; variance-ratio random walk after the change. Old data.
items.quote: We find that reversals became less common after the rule change. The aggregate statistics also show that settlement prices become more efficient after the change.

items.value: WASDE (monthly, 12:00 ET since 2013): price effect not significant at 10 min, significant at 30 min; soybean reaction keeps growing from 30 min to the day close
items.window: 2010-2021, 122 WASDE reports, CME nearby corn and soybean futures
items.detail: Anderson, McKenzie, Noyes (2024) NCCC-134 conference paper (working paper, not peer-reviewed). Event study: return from release (or from the open when released before the open) to +10 min, +30 min and the day close, regressed on WASDE world-ending-stocks surprise vs Bloomberg analyst survey (SUR). Corn: -0.023 (10 min, n.s.), -0.041** (30 min), -0.044* (day). Soybeans: -0.028 (n.s.), -0.061**, -0.124** (day); 10-min vs day coefficients differ significantly for soybeans only. Absorption: slow for soybeans (drift beyond 30 min, surprise-conditional, in sample); corn mostly done by 30 min. Needs the analyst-survey surprise. Contradicts Lehecka et al. 2014 (about 10 min) and Adjemian-Irwin 2018 (few minutes).
items.quote: We do not find a significant market reaction within the first ten minutes after the report release time. However, we do find significant and directionally appropriate price reactions after 30 minutes. Furthermore, the price reaction continues to grow for soybeans between 30 minutes and the daily close.

items.value: major USDA reports: reactions persist about ten minutes; no systematic under- or overreaction
items.detail: Lehecka, Wang, Garcia (2014) Applied Economic Perspectives and Policy 36(3) 504-526 (peer-reviewed). Absorption: within about 10 minutes (mostly before the 2013 move to 11:00 CT releases, when reports came out before the open). Negative for drift. Full text paywalled; abstract only.
items.quote: Strongest price reactions to the releases are found immediately after the market opens, and market reactions persist for approximately ten minutes. The electronic corn futures market quickly incorporates this new public information, and little evidence exists to support systematic under- or overreactions in prices.

items.quote: ensuing real-time trading on USDA crop announcements exhibits noticeable volatility spikes in agricultural futures markets, but that this heightened volatility dissipates within the space of a few trading minutes.

items.detail: de Boer, Gardebroek, Pennings, Trujillo-Barrera (2022) J. Futures Markets (peer-reviewed). Liquidity, not returns: not evidence of price mean reversion. Planner pointer (unverified): round-trip liquidity cost 9.2 bp ZS, 12.5 bp ZL, 13.6 bp ZM. Abstract only.

items.value: first half-hour return positively predicts last half-hour return: DCE soybean slope 0.073 (R2 1.80%), soybean meal slope 0.052 (R2 0.90%), significant at 5%
items.detail: Jin, Kearney, Li, Yang, 'Intraday time-series momentum: Evidence from China', Journal of Futures Markets (2019/2020, peer-reviewed; doi 10.1002/fut.22084); MPRA working paper 97134 (Nov 2019) read in full. Venue: Dalian Commodity Exchange (another venue of the ZS and ZM underlyings). Horizon: first 30 min -> last 30 min of the day; also rest-of-day. In sample (full-sample regressions); trading-strategy returns GROSS of transaction costs. Sign positive (momentum). Only the second-to-last session also predicts for soybean meal; overnight return has power for soybean meal. Data mostly before 2010-2013.
items.quote: We observe that the first 30-minute returns positively predict the last 30-minute returns for all four contracts with a slope of 0.073 for soybean, 0.052 for soybean meal, 0.067 for copper, and 0.103 for steel. All of these are significant at a 5% level. Furthermore, the R2 for these four contracts are 1.80%, 0.90% 1.36% and 3.32%, respectively. ... The returns comparison presented in Table 7 is based on gross returns that do not take transaction costs into account.

items.quote: The percentage of the days in which we reject the null hypothesis of no cointegration is about 70% across all contract pairs for both commodities, suggesting nearby and deferred futures share the same stochastic trend most of the time. ... For corn futures, the nearby contract only slightly dominates the first deferred contract in price discovery with an average price discovery share of 52%. ... By the deferred 4 contract, the nearby price discovery share has reached 78%.
